newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end modestly up, seen firming Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end modestly up, seen firming Tuesday.

text.p: Brazil shares ended slightly higher on increased buying of top blue chips, and analysts expect stocks to open firmer Tuesday, brokers said.
"Considering today's close, we can see the market opening firmer on Tuesday," a senior trader said.

The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded stocks rose 0.51 percent, closing at 65,563 points. Volume was 457.8 million reais ($443 million), of which over 130 million reais were due to a deal involving options and shares of Telebras.

Among blue chips, the big winner was Petrobras preferred, which jumped 4.23 percent to close at 135 reais. The stock was boosted by the company's launch of a Level One ADR program and positive nine-month results, both last week. while Eletrobras gained 0.75 percent to 335.50 reais.
Analysts said investor interest increased today as speculation over Brazil's October trade deficit finally ended with the government's announcement last Thursday of a record $1.3 billion trade gap.

Traders also noted that with municipal elections now over, the market will focus on congressional discussions on the re-election amendment, which would give President Fernando Henrique Cardoso a shot at a second term.

Analysts also noted Sao Paulo state bank Banespa preferred moved on news that an agreement on a restructuring plan for Sao Paulo's debt to the bank will be announced some time soon. Banespa has been under Central Bank administration since December 1994.
Banespa preferred rose 0.19 real to 2.20 reais.
